scientific_limitations_and_integrity.claim_scope: For every nonzero integer n and every integer c, the exceptional family \(F_c(X,Y,Z)=(X+Y)^2+cYZ\) has an explicit integer-polynomial solution x,y,z,t with gcd in \(\mathbb Z[u,v]\) equal to one and \(t^2=nxyzF_c(x,y,z)\).
scientific_limitations_and_integrity.limitations: Only the exceptional coefficient family \(a=d=0,\ b=2\) is treated; the other coefficient cases of Conjecture 2.4(a) remain outside this result. No independent audit has been performed.
scientific_limitations_and_integrity.provenance: Motivated by the explicitly stated gap in Gawron–Ulas, arXiv:1502.07307v1, Remark 2.3 and Conjecture 2.4(a).
scientific_limitations_and_integrity.verification: Exact symbolic polynomial identities were checked by the included standard-library verifier; coprimality is established in the written proof.

title: Primitive polynomial solutions in the exceptional quadratic-form family
